in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Great! Let me start by asking about your child or children.

**How old is your child (or children)?** 

To help determine eligibility, I need to know:
- How many children are you asking about?
- What is each child's date of birth (or their current age)?

This will help me guide you through the appropriate eligibility checks. Child Benefit has different requirements depending on the child's age:
- **Under 16 years old**: Generally qualify
- **16-19 years old**: Must be in approved education or training
- **20 years or over**: Generally do not qualify

Please tell me about your child/children so we can continue.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 21 years old and lives at home with me. I wanted to check if I can still claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for providing that information. Based on what you've told me, I need to let you know about the eligibility outcome for Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to inform you that **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

**Why:**
Child Benefit can only be claimed for children who are:
- Under 16 years old, **OR**
- Aged 16-19 and in approved education or training

Since Alex is 21 years old, he no longer meets the age requirements for Child Benefit eligibility, even though he lives at home with you.

**What this means:**
- Your Child Benefit for Alex would have stopped when he turned 20 (unless he was in full-time education at that time, which would have extended eligibility until the end of the course or age 19, whichever is earlier)
- Once he reached age 20, he no longer qualifies as a "qualifying child"

**Next steps:**
If you believe there may have been a change in circumstances that should have been reported to HMRC, or if you have other children you'd like me to check eligibility for, please let me know. Otherwise, you may want to contact HMRC directly if you have questions about when your claim for Alex should have ended.

Is there anything else I can help you with, or do you have other children you'd like me to check eligibility for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Oh, I see. That's disappointing, but I understand. So once he turned 20, that was it then? Even though he still lives at home with me?

No, Alex is my only child, so I guess that's that. Thank you for explaining it to me clearly though - at least I know where I stand now.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
You're welcome, and I'm glad I could clarify the situation for you.

Yes, that's correct - once Alex turned 20, he no longer qualified as a "qualifying child" for Child Benefit purposes, regardless of the fact that he still lives at home with you. The age limits are quite strict for this benefit, and living arrangements don't change the eligibility rules.
